# C code

Most Kokeb Labs code is C++, but C still appears: C APIs that kb-core keeps for compatibility, MCU vendor code and code
generated by CubeMX or ESP-IDF. These rules say how our own C is written and how vendor and generated C is kept apart.
The C++ rules on heap, errors, integers and static analysis apply to C as well.

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [KB-CC-001](#kb-cc-001) C is C17 without compiler extensions | must | driver, library, hal, firmware, template | planned |
| [KB-CC-002](#kb-cc-002) C headers work from C++ and expose only C types | must | driver, library, hal, firmware, template | planned |
| [KB-CC-003](#kb-cc-003) C names are snake\_case with the repository prefix; file-local functions are static | must | driver, library, hal, firmware, template | planned |
| [KB-CC-004](#kb-cc-004) C APIs return an error enum whose zero is success, and the result is used | must | driver, library, hal, firmware, template | review |

| [KB-CC-006](#kb-cc-006) Generated vendor code is edited only between its user-code markers | must | hal, firmware | planned |
| [KB-CC-007](#kb-cc-007) Vendor and third-party code lives in excluded directories | must | driver, library, hal, firmware, template | review |

## KB-CC-001: C is C17 without compiler extensions { #kb-cc-001 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Our own C sources build as ISO C17 (`CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17`, `CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON`, `CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF`).
Vendor and generated code keeps the standard its supplier uses.

*Why:* Neither source handbook fixed a C standard. The pinned GCC toolchains default to C17 with GNU extensions; turning
the extensions off keeps the code portable to clang on the host.

*Verified by:*

- `forbidden-patterns/cmake-c-standard` (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names
  the pattern set


## KB-CC-002: C headers work from C++ and expose only C types { #kb-cc-002 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

A header that declares a C API wraps its declarations in `extern "C"` guarded by `__cplusplus`, and its signatures use
only C types (`<stdint.h>`, `<stdbool.h>`, plain structs and enums), so C and C++ callers see the same ABI.

*Verified by:*

- `header-self-contained` (planned): every public header compiles on its own as the first include of a translation unit
- review: Each C API header has the extern "C" guard and uses only C types in its signatures.


## KB-CC-003: C names are snake\_case with the repository prefix; file-local functions are static { #kb-cc-003 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. Needs C-specific naming options for `.c` files in place of the C++ ones
    config/.clang-tidy applies today.

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

C functions and variables are `snake_case` and public ones start with the repository prefix (`kb_`, `<chip>_`); typedefs
end in `_t` with that prefix, and enumerators are `UPPER_SNAKE` with the type's prefix. Functions used only in one file
are `static`.

*Why:* C has no namespaces, so the prefix is the namespace. The org `.clang-tidy` naming options are written for C++ and
today also lint `.c` files.

*Verified by:*

- `c-naming` (planned): clang-tidy readability-identifier-naming with C options (snake\_case functions and variables,
  \*\_t typedefs, UPPER\_CASE enumerators, repository prefix) run on .c files and C API headers

*See also:* [ADR-0008](../adr/0008-naming.md)


## KB-CC-004: C APIs return an error enum whose zero is success, and the result is used { #kb-cc-004 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

A C function that can fail returns its module's error enum, with the success value equal to 0, and is declared with
`__attribute__((warn_unused_result))` (or the project's macro for it) so a caller cannot drop the result.

*Verified by:*

- review: Each new fallible C function returns the module's error enum and is marked warn\_unused\_result.

*See also:* [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-error-model.md); SEI CERT C ERR33-C


## KB-CC-005: Every C function has a prototype { #kb-cc-005 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI. The C build must add both flags with -Werror.

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

Every C function is declared with a full prototype (`void f(void)`, never `void f()`), and every function with external
linkage has a prototype in a header before it is defined.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wstrict-prototypes` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `compiler-warnings/-Wmissing-prototypes` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror


## KB-CC-006: Generated vendor code is edited only between its user-code markers { #kb-cc-006 }

**MUST** · hal, firmware · since 1.0

Code generated by CubeMX or another vendor tool is changed only between its `USER CODE BEGIN`/`END` markers; any other
change is recorded in `PATCHES.md` beside it. Regenerating from the committed project file reproduces the committed
code.

*Why:* Changes outside the markers are lost silently at the next regeneration.

*Verified by:*

- `vendor-regen-diff` (planned): CI regenerates vendor code (CubeMX) from the committed project file and fails if the
  result differs from the committed sources outside user-code markers and PATCHES.md
- review: Edits to generated files are inside user-code markers or listed in PATCHES.md.


## KB-CC-007: Vendor and third-party code lives in excluded directories { #kb-cc-007 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

Vendor, generated and third-party sources live under `third_party/`, `external/`, `managed_components/` or the
generator's own directory, which format and lint exclude. Our code is never placed there to avoid the checks.

*Why:* Reformatting vendor code makes every vendor update a conflict, so it is excluded, which only holds if the
exclusion covers vendor code and nothing else.

*Verified by:*

- review: Code written by us is not under an excluded directory.

*See also:* [ADR-0009](../adr/0009-licensing.md)
